soundness_flags.label: Definitions qGauss, fGauss, Gamma; theorems local-action-regret, uniform-second-order-risk, and global-sharp-pilot
soundness_flags.one_line: The limits over |T|→∞ are not indexed by a specified sequence or convergence mode and are not implied uniformly by global empirical-baseline convergence; arbitrary growing subsets can have different covariate compositions, so qGauss, fGauss, Gamma, and hence B are not yet uniquely defined for the asserted uniform claims.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:uniform-second-order-risk and thm:global-sharp-pilot
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The result is conditional on the explicitly narrower likelihood-rich fixed-baseline class M, rather than all deterministic finite-population arrays allowed by Han and Deng.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The second-order expansion and square-root pilot constant are claimed only uniformly over M and its probability-one realized-array subclass.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 8 gives first-order joint asymptotic behavior for the learned factorial procedure; the conclusion states that optimal learning-sample proportion remains an important problem for refined asymptotics.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Appendix E.4, Theorem E.1 and equations (E.4)–(E.6)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves an approximately rate-optimal pooled binary-arm plan with m asymptotic to n^(2/3) and worst-case loss of order n^(-4/3).
The two-stage Bayesian rerandomization analysis takes both stage sizes to infinity with their ratio converging to a constant and gives a first-order PRIASV expression.
The paper studies best-choice Mahalanobis rerandomization, including Berry–Esseen-style large-sample theory with numbers of covariates and candidate randomizations allowed to grow.
The paper develops factorial rerandomization under randomization inference and derives a symmetric truncated-Gaussian asymptotic law for the usual factorial-effect estimators.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace each bare |T|→∞ limit by a specified full-array or random-complement sequence, state uniform-in-beta convergence in probability for G_T and its derivatives, and define the conditional-boundary covariance through a continuous coarea/disintegration version.

Add a worked bounded GLM factorial family that verifies nonempty quotient dimension, constant positive score rank, nuisance orthogonality, and positive Gamma; this would establish that the likelihood-rich class is scientifically attainable rather than merely regular by assumption.
State asymptotic minimaxity for E_n explicitly, for example by defining it through the ratio to inf over admissible balanced pilot sizes, before asserting uniqueness of the pilot-scale limit.

recommended_next_step: Revise the subset-sequence and Gaussian-boundary definitions, then retain this field-tier factorial second-order pilot frontier for Stage 0.
